title: Quercetin: 870 Studies on Natural Anti-Inflammatory Power
abstract:
### Does Quercetin Actually Lower Blood Sugar and Protect Against Diabetes?  
If you've been told that Type 2 diabetes requires lifelong medication management, you need to read this.  
Research published in the [Journal of Nutrition](https://greenmedinfo.com/article/polyphenol-rich-apple-peel-extract-cherry-extract-and-quercetin-modulates-some) examined whether mice fed quercetin-rich apple and cherry extracts could counteract the harmful effects of a high-fat diet. The results? Mice consuming quercetin became just as obese as high-fat-fed mice, but their blood glucose concentrations dropped 36% after food deprivation compared to controls. Serum C-reactive protein—a key inflammation marker—was reduced 29% in quercetin-fed mice.  
A dose-dependent analysis showed that liver cells exposed to quercetin demonstrated significantly decreased lipid accumulation. In other words, quercetin didn't just improve blood sugar—it directly reduced fat storage in liver tissue at the cellular level.
### Can Quercetin Lower Blood Pressure Without Pharmaceutical Side Effects?  
Heart disease kills more Americans than any other condition. And the pharmaceutical answer? Statin drugs, blood pressure medications, and blood thinners—each with its own devastating side effect profiles.  
A systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 randomized controlled trials involving [896 participants](https://greenmedinfo.com/article/quercetin-intake-resulted-significantly-decreased-blood-pressure-humans) examined quercetin supplementation's effects on blood pressure and metabolic markers. The pooled results were striking: quercetin significantly lowered systolic blood pressure by 3.09 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure by 2.86 mmHg.  
In subgroup analyses, participants who consumed quercetin for eight weeks or more showed significantly improved HDL cholesterol and triglyceride levels. No pharmaceutical side effects. No sexual dysfunction. No muscle pain or liver enzyme elevations that come standard with statin drugs.
### What Other Conditions Does Quercetin Address?  
The research on quercetin extends far beyond what we've covered so far.  
[Sepsis](https://greenmedinfo.com/article/quercetin-has-therapeutic-potential-treatment-sepsis)—a severe and often fatal condition affecting 750,000 Americans annually—showed that quercetin administration reduced tissue damage, decreased reactive oxygen species levels, and significantly downregulated High Mobility Group Box 1 protein expression. The findings suggest quercetin has therapeutic potential in treating sepsis when conventional anti-inflammatory drugs fail.  
For those dealing with gout or elevated uric acid, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial found that [500 mg quercetin daily](https://greenmedinfo.com/article/quercetin-lowers-plasma-uric-acid-pre-hyperuricaemic-males) for four weeks significantly lowered plasma uric acid concentrations by 26.5 µmol/L in healthy males with pre-hyperuricemia—without affecting glucose levels or blood pressure.  
Even in [kidney transplant patients](https://greenmedinfo.com/article/bioflavonoid-therapy-curcumin-and-quercetin-improves-cadaveric-renal-transplan), a randomized controlled trial using quercetin and curcumin showed beneficial effects on early graft function, demonstrating these natural compounds' renoprotective and antioxidant properties in one of medicine's most critical interventions.
